title: Apply slice-1 review: exit policy, RenderedSegment, non_exhaustive, edge tests
description: Apply four reviewers' feedback to slice 1 before committing: (1) Parse-failure exit policy: render '?' marker, eprint details, exit SUCCESS (not FAILURE). (2) Introduce RenderedSegment{text} as Segment trait return so slice-2 width/runs/separator additions don't churn segments. (3) Drop .to_string() from io::Error::other for source-chain preservation. (4) #[non_exhaustive] on ParseError for SemVer headroom. (5) Integration tests: exact-byte assertions (no trim_end). close_reason: Slice-1 review feedback applied: (1) Parse-failure exit policy: lib::run now renders '?' to stdout + eprints detail + returns Ok() instead of io::Error::other(err) to caller — statusline never exits FAILURE on malformed payload, only on actual IO failure. (2) RenderedSegment{text} introduced as Segment trait return, marked #[non_exhaustive] for SemVer-safe growth into the full v0.2 struct. (3) ParseError also #[non_exhaustive]. (5) Added tests: worktree name with '/' (verbatim render), empty worktree name (hidden), git_worktree key absent vs null (both treated as None), lib::run degraded-marker path, lib::run happy path with newline assertion. 11 unit + 3 integration = 14 tests pass. mise run check clean. value: linesmith project vision: new AI coding CLI status line tool in Rust (tool-agnostic — supports Claude Code + Qwen Code today, Codex/Copilot when they ship their statusLine APIs). Differentiators: (1) real plugin API via rhai scripting — none exist in ecosystem, all tools hardcode widgets; (2) correctness-first on context %/rate limits/worktree isolation — biggest user pains per research; (3) curated presets for onboarding (Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord/Gruvbox/Tokyo Night/Rose Pine + minimal/default); (4) single-binary (~3-5MB) kills npx supply-chain risk. Architecture: segment/widget system with priority/width hints, file-based caching, async, conditional visibility, sub-composition. GitHub: oakoss/linesmith. Stack: Rust + serde_json + owo-colors + gix + toml + rhai + ureq + lexopt + dialoguer + terminal_size + supports-hyperlinks + cargo-dist.

User demand research for Claude Code statuslines (ranked by signal strength): (1) Rate-limit/plan-usage visibility — 44+ reactions on anthropics/claude-code#8412, loudest single signal. Scrape from API headers like ccusage does. (2) Effort/thinking level visibility — 13+ separate issues, CC doesn't re-emit on /effort change. (3) Accurate context % — breaks in 1M context, post-/compact, post-/resume, during 429s. Table stakes, nobody has nailed it. (4) Worktree isolation — model/state leaks across worktrees, ccstatusline#190. (5) Preset onboarding — ccstatusline#42/#226/#277. (6) Burn-rate + survival projection — AndrewTKent mockup #43271. (7) Live skill/agent/MCP visibility — claude-hud at 19.8k stars proves demand. (8) Cache-hit/cache-creation countdown. Top complaints: npx spawns 30+ processes/3GB RAM (ccstatusline#103, #22, chongdashu PR#4), supply-chain risk of @latest (#298), context % wrong more often than right, rendering brittle across tmux/iTerm/IntelliJ/Windows. Competitors: ccstatusline (7.7k TS dominant), CCometixLine (2.7k Rust/TOML), claude-powerline/Owloops (1k TS), claude-hud (19.8k plugin-style), claudia-statusline (Rust+SQLite), felipeelias (Go/TOML). No tool has real plugin API — biggest architectural gap.

Claude Code statusline API contract: spawned per prompt with 300ms debounce, rich JSON on stdin with model {id, display_name}, cwd, workspace {current_dir, project_dir, added_dirs, git_worktree {name, path}}, context_window {used_percentage, context_window_size, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, current_usage {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}}, cost {total_cost_usd, total_duration_ms, total_api_duration_ms, total_lines_added, total_lines_removed}, rate_limits {five_hour, seven_day — Pro/Max only}, output_style, vim, agent. Plain text stdout, ANSI + OSC 8 hyperlinks, multi-line OK, no timeout. current_usage null before first API call. Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline
